title: Per-tenant admission windows + rolling padding co-scheduler for capacity-safe dedicated upgrades
creator: Lena Cho
description: Introduce a co-scheduling controller that applies per-tenant admission windows and rolling padding to GPU pools during LTS/dedicated fleet upgrades. Goals: avoid large capacity drops, minimize global autoscaler churn, and provide deterministic tenant-level upgrade windows that can be used for compliance, canaries, and rollback.
acceptance_criteria: Controller enforces admission windows per pool and tenant and respects configured padding percentages
Autoscaler integrates with controller via handshake API; no violation of pool-level SLOs observed in staging
Upgrade runbook updated with new checkpoints and emergency rollback triggers
End-to-end test validates zero-violation rollout on synthetic multi-tenant workload
updates: 2026-02-18: RFC drafted; proposed API for admission windows and padding; initial design doc uploaded to Confluence (link in artifacts)
2026-02-25: Spike completed to measure autoscaler reaction time to 10% capacity drain; discovered 12s median stabilization — requires handshake delay
2026-03-02: Prototype co-scheduler implemented in dev cluster; registered as opt-in feature flag `co_scheduler_v1`
2026-03-08: Integration test flake observed when tenant eviction intersects with burst autoscaling; mitigation: introduce eviction grace window per tenant
2026-03-10: PM review accepted rollout gates; preparing canary on two low-risk pools next week
risks: Autoscaler may overreact to transient drains causing oscillation; mitigated by handshake and stabilization window
Per-tenant admission rules increase scheduler complexity and potential for misconfigured tenants to block upgrades; mitigation: validation webhook + dry-run mode
Lack of tenant isolation on shared pools could surface noisy neighbor effects during staged rollouts
test_plan: Unit tests for handshake and padding math
Integration in staging with 50 tenants at production-like qps and request size distribution
Chaos test: inject pod failures during window enforcement
Golden path e2e: schedule upgrade with canary tenant, validate SLOs and automatic rollback
notes: Alternative considered: static 'reserved slots' per tenant but rejected due to poor utilization for bursty tenants
Follow-up: add admission window telemetry to per-tenant billing dashboards to surface capacity inefficiency
